decisions.reason: Connects the session/tool worker to the host installation via the log header, walks npm's remove→fetch→linkStuff trace, explains host death, GUI disconnect, and the never-returned tool result with its outcome preserved as unknown; frames it as a structural self-host hazard, not a network flake, without overgeneralizing across platforms.

Explains content present while dsh/dsh.cmd are missing and dsh.ps1 is stale (dangling pointer into the old tree); ties the hand-swapped nonstandard tree to the broken shims and rejects hand-swapping or hand-writing shims with grounded reasons.

Grounds the repair in repair-notes.md: external pinned npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 regenerating the shims, dsh --version = rc.1 verification, source checkout aligned to dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1 with no unrelated edits; keeps the recorded repair and the proposed verification clearly separated, marking the post-repair boot unconfirmed.

Recognizes the agent is a component of the upgrade target and must hand off, not execute; external procedure fully stops every dsh host before the exact-version install, restarts, hard-refreshes and verifies; distinguishes established stop-first/pinning rules from the self-host refusal rule and excludes a dependent in-host tool worker from counting as an external shell.

Proposes a concrete guard comparing the running host's package root with the command's mutation target plus R-12-style relation checks; uses the version-only alpha.5→rc.1 diff to conclude no plugin re-migration; checklist covers version markers, ghost check, restart/refresh, actual plugin loading, and backup cleanup only after verification, with no code change and conclusions tied to the supplied tags.

caps.reason: Final advice refuses in-session execution and hands over an external procedure run with the host stopped.
Final fix is the formal external pinned install; manual directory swaps and handmade shims are explicitly rejected.
